_**User**_

In C:\Users\graff\WebstormProjects\stepdown-rule, search the TypeScript source (src/, scripts/, tests/) for cross-platform path and shell issues.

Look for:
- path separators hardcoded as '/' or '\\'
- use of `rm`, `cp`, `mv`, `chmod`, `ln`, `which`, `bash`, `sh -c`
- `process.env.HOME` without USERPROFILE
- `os.tmpdir` vs /tmp
- `child_process` spawn/exec with shell assumptions
- `fs` ops that fail on Windows (symlinks, executable bits)
- file URL / import.meta.url path handling
- CRLF vs LF assumptions in tests
- any existing process.platform or path.win32 usage

Return file:line references and brief notes on Windows impact. Do NOT modify files.

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
A path join involving `tmpDir` and a glob pattern was flagged as problematic.

`FileService.normalizePattern` hardcodes forward slashes, which corrupts Windows paths like `C:\foo` when joined with backslashes. `minimatch` defaults to slash-based separators, so Windows backslash paths may fail to match ignore patterns unless escape options are configured.

`cli.ts` uses a `#!/usr/bin/env bun` shebang, which may fail on Windows. The compiled output path `./dist/stepdown-rule` omits the `.exe` extension, though Bun usually appends it automatically on Windows.
</details></think>

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
An interesting finding was spotted in package.json.

package.json contains a `rm -rf` script that hardcodes Unix shell commands. The `postbuild` script also invokes `bun` with `--shell`, assuming a Unix-like environment. These are adjacent issues rather than inside the requested `src/`, `scripts/`, or `tests/` directories.

The `bin` entry omits `.exe`, which breaks Windows npm bin resolution. The glob package may return forward slashes on Windows, causing `file-service.test.ts:27` to fail its `join(tmpDir, "app.ts")` assertion.

A path normalization bug exists in `normalizePattern`. It checks `pattern.endsWith("/")` to append `/**/`. On Windows this fails for backslash paths. A directory like `C:\temp\foo` becomes `C:\temp\foo/**/*.ts` with mixed slashes. A trailing backslash produces `C:\temp\foo\/**/*.ts`.

Minimatch lacks Windows path normalization. Glob returns backslashes on Windows, but ignore patterns use forward slashes. This causes mismatches against `**/skip.ts`.

TypeScript printer forces LF. Reading CRLF files and splitting on `\n` leaves carriage returns on lines. This breaks equality checks and string comparisons.

Movement counting and preview diffs can expose `\r` artifacts when trimmed lines still contain carriage returns.

cli.test.ts expects the exact fixture path `fixtures/test-violations.ts`. If glob normalizes Windows paths differently, this assertion will fail.

Git `core.autocrlf` settings affect whether fixture files arrive with CRLF or LF line endings.

`Bun.spawnSync` receives an argv array, so it avoids shell assumptions. The `Bun.$` template in `build.ts` relies on Unix-style paths and symlinks. `bun build --compile` emits the binary without `.exe`, which Windows normally expects. `process.env.HOME` is absent from the source.

`os.tmpdir()` is used correctly throughout the source. There is no hardcoded `/tmp` or `process.platform`/`path.win32` logic anywhere. `child_process` is not used; `Bun.spawnSync` is preferred. File operations such as `chmod` and symlinks appear only in comments, not in active code.

The rule-validator EXCLUDE_PATTER normalizes backslashes to forward slashes before appending trailing slashes. This provides correct Windows path handling. Whether glob needs `windowsPathsNoEscape` is still being verified.
</details></think>

## Cross-platform audit (`src/`, `scripts/`, `tests/`)

No `process.platform`, `path.win32`, `process.env.HOME`, hardcoded `/tmp`, `child_process`, `chmod`, or symlink FS ops found. Real risks below.

---

### High / likely Windows impact

| Location | Issue | Windows impact |
|---|---|---|
| `src/services/FileService.ts:49-50` | Dir→glob uses hardcoded `/` and `endsWith("/")` only | Absolute Windows dirs (`C:\foo` or trailing `\`) become mixed/`\\/**` patterns; may miss files or confuse `glob` |
| `src/services/FileService.ts:59,64` | Ignore/minimatch patterns use `/`; no `windowsPathsNoEscape` / path normalize | User `--ignore` / built-in `**/node_modules/**` can fail to match `\` paths from `glob` |
| `tests/idempotency.test.ts:122` | `join(tmpDir, "src", "**", "*.ts")` | On win32 `join` turns this into `...\src\**\*.ts`; `**` as path segment can break glob matching |
| `src/fixer.ts:502` | Printer forced to `NewLineKind.LineFeed` | Fix always rewrites CRLF sources to LF |
| `src/fixer.ts:228,241` + `src/cli-output.ts:142-153` | `split("\n")` / `join("\n")` | CRLF leaves `\r` on lines → movement counts / preview diffs skewed; LF rewrite can make `fixed !== original` even with no AST change |
| `scripts/build.ts:34` | `--outfile ./dist/stepdown-rule` (no `.exe`) | Compile on Windows typically yields `stepdown-rule.exe`; bin name mismatch |
| `src/cli.ts:1` | `#!/usr/bin/env bun` | Fine under `bun …`; useless / confusing if run as native script on Windows |

---

### Medium

| Location | Issue | Windows impact |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/cli.test.ts:5,8-88` | `Bun.spawnSync(["bun", …])` + argv globs like `fixtures/.../**/*.ts` | OK if `bun` on PATH (no shell). Exact `toBe("fixtures/test-violations.ts")` assumes `/` path strings from resolver |
| `tests/file-service.test.ts:27,54` | `expect(files).toEqual([join(tmpDir, …)])` | Fails if `glob` returns `/` while `join` returns `\` |
| `tests/helpers.ts:84` + many tests | Literal `fixtures/...` with `/` | Usually OK with Bun/`glob`; cwd-relative, not drive-letter aware |
| `scripts/rule-validator.ts:83` | `split("\n")` for line numbers | CRLF → `\r` still in line text; columns/messages slightly off |
| `scripts/build.ts:32-33` | Comments assume Unix symlink/`~/bin`/`/usr/local/bin` | Docs/intent only; distribution story is Unix-centric |
| `src/cli.ts:183`, `src/cli-runners.ts:67`, `src/cli-options.ts:5-10` | Shell quoting hints / default `src/**/*.ts` | PowerShell/cmd glob expansion differs from bash; quoting advice still valid |

---

### Low / mostly OK

| Location | Note |
|---|---|
| `src/services/FileService.ts:2,68-69` | Uses `resolve` + `sep` for write guard — correct Windows segment split |
| `tests/file-service.test.ts:3,10` | Uses `os.tmpdir()` — correct (no `/tmp`) |
| `tests/helpers.ts:17-27` | `path.join` + `rmSync`/`mkdirSync` — portable |
| `tests/idempotency.test.ts:2,120` | `cpSync`/`existsSync` (Node FS), not shell `cp` |
| `scripts/rule-validator.ts:10-11` | Normalizes `\`→`/` before exclude checks — good |
| `scripts/build.ts:7-28` | `./dist/...` path strings — Bun accepts `/` on Windows |
| Fixture/path strings throughout tests | Forward-slash relative paths; typically fine under Bun |

---

### Not found (in scoped TS)

- `process.env.HOME` without `USERPROFILE`
- Hardcoded `/tmp`
- `child_process` / `shell: true` / `sh -c` / `bash` / `which` / `chmod` / `ln`
- Shell `rm`/`cp`/`mv` in TS (only Node `rmSync`/`cpSync`)
- `fileURLToPath` / `import.meta.url` (tests use Bun `import.meta.dir` at `tests/cli.test.ts:5`)
- Any `process.platform` / `path.win32` branching

---

### Adjacent (outside TS dirs, still Windows-breaking)

| Location | Issue |
|---|---|
| `package.json:35` | `"remove-buildinfo": "rm -rf …"` — fails in cmd.exe unless Bun shell wraps it |
| `package.json:21` | `"bin": "./dist/stepdown-rule"` — no `.exe` for Windows binaries |

---

### Summary

Biggest code risks: **FileService separator assumptions**, **idempotency `join(...,"**",...)`**, **LF-only fix pipeline vs CRLF**, **compile/bin without `.exe`**. Platform detection is absent everywhere — no win32 special-casing today.
